sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Reform UK Suspends MP Jason Powell for Concentration Camp Advocacy
cards.content: An aspiring Reform UK MP, Jason Powell, has been suspended from the party after advocating for concentration camps and stating that Muslims cannot be British. Powell's comments were recorded in an ITV documentary, which also featured other party members expressing extreme views. One councillor, Dean Miller, was recorded calling for King Charles to be beheaded because he believed the king was secretly a Muslim, leading Conservative, Labour, and Liberal Democrat councillors to call for his resignation. The Muslim Council of Britain criticized Reform UK's leadership for allowing a culture of hatred to fester within the organization. Reform UK has suspended Powell, but critics argue that the party's vetting process is flawed, allowing extreme views to be expressed.

cards.title: Austrian Airlines Flight Makes Emergency Landing in Bulgaria
cards.content: An Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna was forced to make an emergency landing in Sofia, Bulgaria, after a reported bomb threat. The Airbus A320 plane was traveling with 51 passengers and six crew members when it was diverted to Sofia, where passengers were evacuated. The Bulgarian air force scrambled a MiG-29 fighter jet to escort the airliner. So far, no injuries have been reported, and an investigation has begun. The incident comes after a recent attempt to hijack a Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv, and similar incidents have occurred in the past, including a false hijacking alert on a commercial flight from Corfu to Nuremberg.

cards.title: US Allows Ukrainians, Sudanese to Keep Deportation Protections
cards.content: The US Department of Homeland Security announced that Ukrainian and Sudanese immigrants who were facing deportation protections expiration will be allowed to continue living and working in the country for now. This decision applies to over 100,000 Ukrainians and nearly 1,800 Sudanese nationals who were enrolled in the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program. The protection for both countries was set to expire on Monday, but the agency will make an announcement at a later time. Until then, immigrants from Ukraine and Sudan who are currently in the US will retain their protections. The decision comes as the Trump administration has repeatedly terminated TPS for multiple countries, citing it as a temporary solution, not a permanent one. The US Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to end TPS for Haitians and Syrians in June, leaving those who lost their status vulnerable to detention and deportation.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: World Edges Closer to 30% Land Conservation Goal, Gaps Remain
cards.content: A recent study suggests that the world may be closer to achieving its 30% land conservation goal, but significant gaps in grassland and shrubland protection remain. These areas, which support unique wildlife, are not fully represented in global conservation records, indicating that simply expanding the total area of protected land is not enough to ensure the conservation of all wildlife habitats. The study highlights the need for more effective management of conservation areas and a focus on improving the overall effectiveness of conservation efforts to meet the 30% target and address the biodiversity crisis.

cards.title: White dwarfs have unexpected colors, including green, pink, and purple, study finds.
cards.content: In a groundbreaking study, astronomers from the University of Warwick have discovered that white dwarfs, the remnants of stars that have reached the end of their life, can have unexpected colors. Unlike most stars which change color based on their temperature, white dwarfs can have shades of green, pink, and purple. The researchers found that this unusual coloration is caused by the interaction of trace elements in the star's atmosphere with the surrounding dense helium plasma. The team used spectra collected by astronomers to calculate how each star's light would appear to human eyes, revealing that some white dwarfs can appear green, yellow, pink, or purple due to the enrichment of their atmospheres with elements from rocky debris. The study suggests that about one in thirty white dwarfs across the Universe could have unusual coloring, with some stars being even more vibrantly colored than others.

cards.title: Pittsburgh Businessman's AI-Powered Wearables Raise Privacy Concerns
cards.content: Chris Thomas, a Pittsburgh-based business owner and livestreamer, uses AI-powered devices to record his daily life, raising concerns about privacy and consent. Thomas wears camera-equipped glasses, a note-taking pendant, and a wristband that record his activities. He has encountered situations where bystanders feel uncomfortable knowing they are being recorded, and Thomas removes the devices or turns them off. The article discusses the potential erosion of privacy, citing the devices' ability to continuously listen, interpret speech, and extract meaning without retaining the underlying audio. It also highlights the legal questions surrounding these devices, with some state laws defining interception broadly. The article concludes that the growing use of AI-powered devices is changing the privacy landscape, making it more important for individuals to have control over how they interact with technology and to consider the potential risks and consequences.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Losartan Medication Activates Brown Fat for Better Cardiovascular Health
cards.content: A new study on a blood pressure medication, Losartan, reveals that it could have a second use in activating brown fat, a tissue that burns energy to produce heat and is linked to better cardiovascular health. The research, published in Nature, analyzed medical records and PET/CT scans of over 100,000 patients and found that patients taking Losartan were more likely to have brown fat detected on their scans. The study also found that Losartan directly increased metabolic activity in brown fat cells and had a positive effect on the body's energy-burning fat. This discovery could lead to future treatments for people with normal blood pressure, as well as potential benefits for cardiovascular health. Additionally, the study found that brown fat was associated with lower rates of anxiety and depression, and its activity was linked to several health indicators, including blood sugar regulation, blood fats, and heart function. The researchers noted that further study is needed to fully understand the connections between brown fat and these health outcomes.

cards.title: Experimental treatment shows promise against C. difficile
cards.content: Experimental treatment for C. difficile gut infections, which is caused by an imbalance in the gut's microbial community, has shown promise in early laboratory and mouse research. The treatment, argyrin B, specifically kills the C. difficile bacteria while sparing the rest of the gut microbiome. Researchers have found that argyrin B is highly effective against C. difficile infections, reducing the bacterial load in laboratory experiments and mouse models. The compound acts by targeting a specific antibacterial site in the C. difficile bacteria and has shown little to no effect on beneficial microorganisms in the digestive tract. This could lead to a treatment that reduces the risk of further microbiome disruption, infections, and relapses, and may provide an alternative to the current treatment, fecal microbiota transfer, which is complex and unpleasant for many patients.

cards.title: Fat Before Carbs Regulates Blood Sugar in Mice Study
cards.content: In a breakthrough study, researchers found that eating fat before carbohydrates can help regulate blood sugar levels by slowing down stomach emptying and reducing the initial spike. This effect was observed in mice and may be applicable to humans, offering a potential dietary strategy to manage post-meal blood sugar rises, an important treatment target in diabetes.

cards.title: Avalanche Sweeps Away Over 100 Sheep in Himachal Pradesh
cards.content: In October 2025, Joginder Chand, a 50-year-old shepherd from Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district, set out to migrate his 600 sheep and goats to warmer grazing grounds in Kangra district. Suddenly, an avalanche swept away over 100 animals.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Sunderland Music City gets £156,166 grant for heritage project
cards.content: A major heritage project, Sunderland Music City's Mackem Music Memories, has been awarded £156,166 by the National Lottery Heritage Fund to preserve the city's musical history. The project aims to collect over 300 memories of Sunderland's music scene from residents past and present through questionnaires, research, and interviews. The memories will be displayed in an exhibition at the Culture House Sunderland in summer 2027, along with community activities and live events. The project will also work with diverse communities, including South Asian, Filipino, Nigerian, and Eastern European groups, and international students. The goal is to capture these stories before they disappear and make them part of Sunderland's permanent heritage.

cards.title: Paul Shipper: From Film Fan to Illustrator of Marvel and Star Wars
cards.content: Paul Shipper, a film fan-turned-illustrator, has come a long way from creating movie poster artwork for fun. He has worked on some of Hollywood's biggest franchises, including Marvel, Indiana Jones, and Star Wars. Shipper's passion for illustration started when he was a kid, inspired by the films of George Lucas and Steven Spielberg. He shared his designs online, which led to opportunities that once seemed like a dream. The illustrator has worked on various projects, including posters and artwork for blockbuster titles, and has maintained a consistent artistic style despite working across different projects. Shipper is now involved in a charity exhibition, AMPjam Presents: We've Been Framed, which brings together more than 60 artists from around the world to create original artworks inspired by films and television shows.

cards.title: Scottish Actor Hopes Fans Accept His Accent in Marvel Series
cards.content: Scottish actor Ruaridh Mollica, who plays Tommy Maximoff in the Marvel Cinematic Universe miniseries VisionQuest, hopes fans will accept his Scottish accent. He says speaking in his own accent helped him bring the character to life, and he's excited to be part of the show.

cards.title: EU urged to lift Ukrainian steel restrictions, citing war context
cards.content: The CEO of Metinvest, Ukraine's largest steel company, has urged the European Union to lift restrictions on Ukrainian steel products, claiming they were unfairly bundled with cheaper imports from countries like China. cards.title: Tesla Unveils Electric Sports Car with Hover Capabilities
cards.content: Tesla unveiled a new electric sports car that can hover and turn in mid-air, but it's unclear when flying cars will become a reality. Other news includes Meta's trial over claims its platforms are addictive, a ban on under-16s using social media, and the release of Nintendo's Switch 2. SpaceX's Starship rocket exploded during a test, and the US president is considering selling his Tesla car. A digital detox expert shares tips to help you stop looking at your phone.

cards.title: Small businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence tools
cards.content: Small businesses are adopting AI tools for customer support, marketing, document processing and data analysis. Lower-cost AI services are making technologies that were previously available mainly to large companies more accessible to smaller firms.
